text: A wave starts at the first release of its first epic: Wave 1 at E1, Wave 2 at E2, Wave 3 at E4 and Wave 4 at E6; each of the eight monthly releases keeps its own date, so E3, E5, E7 and E8 close the wave they sit in.
why: Architecture v5 registers four service waves plus Wave 0 while the plan releases once a month, and no source states which release opens a wave; the first release of the wave's first epic is the only boundary both sources support.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 38; Template and Rules R5.6, R5.7; Release Plan v4 Releases and Calendar sheets
applied_in: Waves sheet; Releases sheet note rows; Release rules 9
confirm: Delivery lead with the solution architect
impact: No date moves; a reader knows which releases a service is created in and which releases only add stories to an existing service.

text: Wave 0 has no release of its own: the platform enablers of the seven platform epics complete by the E1 go decision, 27 November 2026 (tentative), inside the E1 window that starts on 2 November 2026 (tentative).
why: Version 4 starts at E1 and no source gives a platform completion date; the E1 go decision is the last date on which the platform can be late without moving a release.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 38; Template and Rules R5.1, R5.6; Release Plan v4 Releases sheet row E1
confirm: Delivery lead with the platform team
impact: A platform enabler that misses 27 November 2026 puts the E1 release at risk; no separate platform release is planned.

text: Gate G7 Contract published is added to the plan: the OpenAPI, AsyncAPI and activity contracts of a service are published with fakes and the contract test runs in every build before a consumer starts, and the gate is decided by the code owner of the owning service with the solution architect.
why: Contract first and the non-blocking class C dependency need a published contract, and version 4 has no gate for it; no source names a contract approver, so the decider is taken from the roles the run already uses.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11; Template and Rules R5.4, R5.7; Release Plan v4 Gates sheet
applied_in: Gates sheet row G7; Release rules 11; Waves sheet entry column
confirm: Solution architect with the TechX tech leads
impact: A consumer service can start on Day 1 against the fake; a service without a published contract holds its consumers but never the wave.

text: The Features and Stories counts and the 'Delivered in' text of version 4 are kept exactly as they stand and are read as monolith-era counts; the realigned counts per release come from the Service Story Catalog v1, the RTM and the Test Cases set, not from this sheet.
why: The counts are source values and no source gives a per-service or per-wave count; rewriting them would invent numbers that no run output yet supports.
read: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json stats; Release Plan v4 Releases and Modules by release sheets; Template and Rules R8.7
applied_in: Releases sheet note row; Modules by release sheet note row; Read me sheet
confirm: Business analyst with the delivery lead
impact: Capacity and benefit planning must take the realigned counts from the story catalog; the plan's own counts stay a legacy baseline.

text: Release readiness is owned by the service owner codes of the Ownership Map v1 for the services of the wave, and the story work by the team types of Template and Rules R5.3; no person is named, and the accountable release owner role is carried open.
why: The plan has no owner column and no source states who owns readiness across a wave; the Ownership Map is the only owner list of the run and rule 4 forbids naming people.
read: Ownership Map v1 Services sheet; Template and Rules R5.3, U3; AGENTS.md rule 4; Release Plan v4 Releases and Gates sheets
applied_in: Waves sheet notes; Services by release sheet; Releases sheet note row
impact: A release has delivery owners per service but no single named accountable role until the position is confirmed.

text: Version 5 is issued as Draft with no recorded approval; the per-epic status words of the source stay as they stand (E1 and E2 Confirmed, E3 to E8 Proposed).
why: The realignment run takes no approval stop and the source records none for the plan, so Draft is the only truthful label.
read: AGENTS.md rule 9; Template and Rules U8, R8.1; Release Plan v4 Releases sheet Status column
applied_in: Read me sheet status line; Releases sheet kept unchanged
impact: The plan can be used for build and review; it cannot be cited as an approved baseline until the approval is recorded.

text: The change log of version 5 starts at version 4 as the source row and records version 4's missing change log and tool line as a gap; the version 4 date 15 November 2026 is kept.
why: Template and Rules R8.1 requires a change-log row and the source has none; recording the gap is better than inventing the history of versions 1 to 4.
read: Template and Rules R8.1, R8.2; workbook properties of version 4 (created 27 October 2026, modified 15 November 2026)
impact: The history before version 4 is not reconstructed; a reader who needs it must go to the earlier files and the document properties.

text: S4 rwb-litigation stays a Wave 3 service with its E2 notice approval work kept in E2 under the W-MAP rule; the service is created for that work at the start of Wave 2 and its remaining work lands in E5.
why: The source gives S4 work in E2 and Architecture v5 creates S4 in Wave 3; R5.6 keeps the business-epic wave for the story and asks for the conflict to be recorded rather than resolved silently, and a removal of S4 from E2 would change the source content.
